Appreciate the quick follow. Attaching the Order Form with our in-house redlines. High level: we need clear title to outputs that are used in our patient-facing product flows (so we can ship features built on top of LLM outputs) and a right to use customer-provided prompts/data to fine-tune closed models internally. Team — forwarding Clearpath’s redlines (see attached). They’re asking for: assignment of output for productized features + broader rights to use customer data for fine-tuning.

High-priority asks from my side:
- Can Legal propose a compromise that protects Redwood model IP and training algos but gives Clearpath the functional rights their product team needs?
- We should consider a field-of-use carveout: assignment/assignment-like rights limited to a named product/workflow (e.g., "Clearpath Patient Assistant"), with a nonexclusive license elsewhere.
- For training: propose a two-track approach — (a) opt-in explicit training consent for fine-tuning (customer can enable), (b) aggregated/derivative feedback license for safety improvements and telemetry.

I’ve sketched a short summary doc that frames our position and risk trade-offs: MSA_Compromise_Suggested_Language.docx (attached). Please review; Ben/Marissa, any commercial flexibility (discount/credits) if we soften the training grant?

Thanks — need an approved draft to send back to Amelia by Wed EOD if we want to close Feb.

—Jordan

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>, ben.carter@redwood-inference.com, marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clearpath redlines — quick internal sync

Jordan / team — thanks for the summary and the suggested language. Quick notes from Legal: we should avoid any broad assignment of model outputs. Assignment of "customer-specific artifacts" that are exact verbatim transcripts could be acceptable but we must preserve Redwood’s pre-existing model weights and training pipelines. Recommended compromise language (high level):

1) Output title: Clearpath receives a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, exclusive right to use, reproduce, and distribute "Customer-Generated Product Content" solely within the named product(s) identified in the Order Form. For clarity, Redwood retains ownership of models, model weights, and any derivatives created as part of Redwood’s broader model improvements.

2) Training/data use: Offer two options in the Order Form —
   - Option A (default): Redwood may use anonymized/aggregated feedback and telemetry for service quality improvements; Clearpath may opt-in to capacity-based fine-tuning (separate managed service, charged) with an explicit dataset contribution and DSAT/retention guarantees.
   - Option B (if customer insists): a limited license permitting Redwood to use de-identified outputs for safety/bug fixes only, with strict retention windows.

3) Audit & safety: Add an evidence clause: for productization of outputs Redwood will provide a certification process (sample evidence) showing no leakage of Redwood proprietary training data.

Commercial ask: if we provide an opt-in fine-tuning path + fielded assignment for named product(s), we should request a modest uplift (recommend 10–15% surcharge or a usage-credit commitment). Ben/Marissa — can you confirm if that’s feasible?

I’ll draft the exact clause text by EOD Friday and we can send to Amelia.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>

Cc: Claire Choi <claire.choi@clearpathhealth.com>, procurement@clearpathhealth.com, laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com, ben.carter@redwood-inference.com
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed compromise language & next steps (Order Form + MSA)

Amelia —

Thanks for the redlines and patience while we reviewed internally. Quick summary of the compromise Redwood can accept:

- Output/productization: Clearpath will receive a perpetual, worldwide right to use, reproduce and distribute Customer-Generated Product Content for the named product(s) listed in Section 1 of the Order Form ("Clearpath Patient Assistant" and identified integrations). This right is limited to the customer product(s) and does not transfer ownership of Redwood model weights, base models, or Redwood tooling.

- Training/feedback: Redwood will offer an explicit opt-in fine-tuning service (paid, separate SOW) where Clearpath can contribute labeled data; otherwise Redwood may only use aggregated and de-identified telemetry for service improvements. If Clearpath requires limited use for safety fixes only, we will accept that under Option B (de-identified + 30-day retention for raw traces).

- Commercials: for the fine-tuning option and productization carveout, Redwood proposes a 12% uplift on committed usage or a $25k annual usage-credit toward dedicated capacity (choose one).

If that captures Clearpath’s needs, our counsel La ura has prepared redline language and I can push the Order Form to DocuSign after you confirm.

Next steps: please reply with either (A) confirm and we’ll route to DocuSign, or (B) request a 1:1 legal call this week with Laura and me to finalize wording.

Link to the proposed sign flow: https://www.docusign.com/clearpath-rd-2027

Appreciate the urgency — hoping to close this week.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
